cards.explanation: The reason Nebuzaradan gives is that the people sinned and did not obey the LORD. He's Babylon's captain of the guard, and he says, "Because you people have sinned against the LORD and have not obeyed His voice, this thing has happened to you." He also says the LORD has done just as He said. The captain spells out the cause himself, friends.

The answer is False. Nebuzaradan says, "If it pleases you to come with me to Babylon, then come, and I will take care of you." Then he adds, "But if it seems wrong to you to come with me to Babylon, go no farther." Nothing forces Jeremiah either way, friends. The chains are off and the choice is his.

The answer is that Nebuzaradan says he will take care of Jeremiah. He says, "If it pleases you to come with me to Babylon, then come, and I will take care of you." That's the whole offer, friends. No job title, no property, just that he'll look after Jeremiah.

The answer is Babylon. Nebuzaradan says Gedaliah is the one "…whom the king of Babylon has appointed over the cities of Judah…" Gedaliah got his post from the king of Babylon. That's how Nebuzaradan describes it, right as he points Jeremiah toward Gedaliah.

The answer is gift. The text says, "Then the captain of the guard gave him a ration and a gift and released him." So Jeremiah leaves with food for the road and a present besides. That's a better send-off than most of us get from a job, friends.

The answer is False. Jeremiah did not go to Babylon. The text says, "So Jeremiah went to Gedaliah son of Ahikam at Mizpah and stayed with him among the people who were left in the land." Babylon was on the table, and he went to Mizpah instead. I think that tells you plenty about where he wanted to be.
The answer is True. Verse 8 says they "…came to Gedaliah at Mizpah…" and they brought their men along. The commanders heard about Gedaliah and went to him. Mizpah is where Gedaliah is staying.

The answer is serving the Babylonians. Gedaliah tells the commanders and their men, "Do not be afraid to serve the Chaldeans. Live in the land and serve the king of Babylon, and it will go well with you." The Chaldeans are the Babylonians, friends. He swore an oath to say it.

The answer is that he will represent them before the Chaldeans. Gedaliah says, "As for me, I will stay in Mizpah to represent you before the Chaldeans who come to us." So when the Babylonians come around, he's the one who speaks for them. That's his job at Mizpah.

The answer is that they return to Judah. The text says "…they all returned from all the places to which they had been banished and came to the land of Judah, to Gedaliah at Mizpah." They had heard the king of Babylon left a remnant and appointed Gedaliah. So they came home, friends.

The answer is kill. Johanan, son of Kareah and one of the army commanders, and the others ask Gedaliah, "Are you aware that Baalis king of the Ammonites has sent Ishmael son of Nethaniah to take your life?" Taking his life means killing him. That's the warning they bring.

The answer is False, friends. The text says it straight: "But Gedaliah son of Ahikam did not believe them." The commanders told him Ishmael had been sent to take his life, and Gedaliah didn't believe it. He didn't buy the warning.
The answer is that Johanan offers to go and kill Ishmael. He says, "Let me go and kill Ishmael son of Nethaniah…" He adds, "No one will know it." That's his offer, friends, and he makes it privately.

The word is perish. Johanan asks, "Why should he take your life and scatter all the people of Judah who have gathered to you, so that the remnant of Judah would perish?" The remnant is the people who are left. He's saying the stakes reach well beyond Gedaliah.
The answer is True. Gedaliah answers Johanan with, "Do not do such a thing!" Then he says, "What you are saying about Ishmael is a lie." So he turns down the offer and calls the claim a lie, friends.
